physicalNotes: Radius 0.43113644 Jupiter radii from Dattilo et al. 2025 (2025AJ....170..318D), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025AJ....170..318D/abstract): 30,822.8 km at 71,492 km per Jupiter radius. GM from the mass 0.0655 Jupiter masses (the NASA Exoplanet Archive's calculated value (M-R relationship, its Chen & Kipping 2017 mass-radius relationship): a model, not a measurement, via the NASA Exoplanet Archive, https://exoplanetarchive.ipac.caltech.edu/docs/pscp_calc.html) times JPL's Jupiter GM. A sphere: no oblateness is measured.

sources.period: Dattilo et al. 2025 (2025AJ....170..318D), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname DATTILO_ET_AL_2025): P 8.538878 d
sources.shape: Dattilo et al. 2025 (2025AJ....170..318D), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname DATTILO_ET_AL_2025): a/R* 16.5649; Dattilo et al. 2025 (2025AJ....170..318D), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname DATTILO_ET_AL_2025): inclination 87.2 degrees
sources.eccentricity: No archive row states an eccentricity; the orbit is taken as circular
sources.phase: Dattilo et al. 2025 (2025AJ....170..318D), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname DATTILO_ET_AL_2025): transit mid-time 2458798.0657 BJD, taken as BJD_TDB; with its period, the row that predicts 2026-01-01 best (1 sigma 3 min)
sources.orientation: Display convention: transit photometry does not measure the orbit's position angle on the sky, so the ascending node is set at position angle 0 (celestial north).
